chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Husayn ibn 'Umara, from Mis'mam, Abu Sayyar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind brothers and sisters from the mother and a grandfather. He said: 'The grandfather is in the position of the paternal brother; he gets two-thirds, and the brothers and sisters from the mother get one-third, so they are equal partners in it.'

key_terms.إِخْوَةً وَأَخَوَاتٍ لِأُمٍّ: Brothers and sisters from the mother (maternal siblings)
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: In the position of / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance share of a grandfather when there are maternal siblings present?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific case where a grandfather inherits alongside maternal siblings (ikhwah wa akhawat min al-umm), ruling that the grandfather receives two-thirds while the maternal siblings share one-third. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the grandfather is treated as a 'hajib' (excluder) of higher degree than maternal siblings but does not exclude them entirely, unlike in some Sunni schools where he may exclude them completely in the presence of other heirs. The distribution reflects the distinct shares assigned to each class of heirs under the *Fara'id* system, emphasizing the grandfather's elevated status relative to the maternal kin.
